title: Can Agentic Trading Systems Pay for Their Own Intelligence?
abstract: arXiv:2607.10286v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used in trading systems, where model reasoning, tool use, and continual decisions incur costs that are expected to produce trading value. Existing evaluations typically report performance metrics, but rarely examine agentic viability: whether dynamic LLM-mediated decisions convert their induced costs into measurable incremental profit. To apply this criterion, we introduce TradeLens, a trace-grounded diagnostic toolkit for evaluating agentic trading systems from their trading records, runtime traces, and deployment configurations. It reconstructs trading trajectories, attributes profit and cost to interpretable evidence, and diagnoses whether and why an agent pays for its own intelligence. translated_title: 智能体交易系统能否为自己付出的智能买单？
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体在交易系统中的应用日益增多，其中模型推理、工具使用和持续决策所产生的成本预期会转化为交易价值。现有评估通常只报告性能指标，却很少检验智能体的可行性：即动态的LLM中介决策能否将其引发的成本转化为可衡量的增量利润。为应用这一标准，我们推出了TradeLens，一个基于交易记录、运行时轨迹和部署配置来评估智能体交易系统的溯源诊断工具包。它重建交易轨迹，将利润和成本归因于可解释的证据，并诊断智能体是否以及为何能为自己付出的智能买单。我们在骨干模型、资金规模、交易频率和系统架构等维度上进行了广泛分析，并附带部署层面的讨论。我们的结果表明，可行性取决于……
tldr: 该论文提出TradeLens工具包，通过重建交易轨迹并将利润与成本归因于可解释证据，来诊断基于LLM的智能体交易系统能否将自身推理成本转化为可衡量的增量利润。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TradeLens, a trace-grounded diagnostic toolkit that reconstructs trading trajectories and attributes profit and cost to interpretable evidence, in order to diagnose whether LLM-based agentic trading systems can convert their own intelligence costs into measurable incremental profit.
